title: DGFT Extends Rice Export Inspection Exemption for Non-EU Europe to April 2027
case_name: DGFT Notification No. 47/2026-27 amending the export policy condition for Basmati and Non-Basmati rice (HSN 1006)
citation: DGFT Notification No. 47/2026-27 dated 9 November 2026, amending Notification No. 07/2026-27 dated 10 April 2026
card_summary: DGFT's Notification No. 47/2026-27, effective immediately from 9 November 2026, keeps the Certificate of Inspection requirement for Basmati and Non-Basmati rice exports limited to EU states, the UK, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland. For every other European destination, exporters stay exempt from producing an EIC/EIA inspection certificate, an exemption now extended from 1 October 2026 to 1 April 2027.
card_tip: A rice exporter shipping to a European country outside the EU, UK, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland needs no EIC/EIA inspection certificate before 1 April 2027; check the buyer's country each shipment.
verification_notes: AUDIENCE: domestic (Indian rice exporters), with a secondary foreign-company angle for European buyers of Indian rice who are affected by the documentation their supplier must produce. TARGET QUERY: do I need an inspection certificate to export rice to Europe. DEMAND EVIDENCE: none seen. Cross-verified across The Tribune, Taxscan, TeamLease RegTech and A2Z Taxcorp, which agree the notification is numbered 47/2026-27, dated 9 November 2026, amends the export policy condition for Basmati and Non-Basmati rice under HSN 1006 (Notification No. 07/2026-27 dated 10 April 2026), takes immediate effect, and extends the Certificate-of-Inspection exemption for non-EU, non-UK European destinations from 1 October 2026 to 1 April 2027, while the requirement continues for EU states, the UK, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland. No source disagreement was seen on these points; the primary DGFT notification text itself was not opened in this run, so the circular number and date rest on the four secondary reports above.
